hypothesis: Distant window cells smaller than two pixels are point-sampled per cell, so which cell a pixel lands in changes as the camera moves. Fading each per-cell random to its expected value once the footprint passes half a cell per pixel should reduce the visible shimmer on distant facades without moving block-average brightness.

provenance.origin: The V2-3b diagnostic edit to scene.frag of 2026-09-11, reverted at the time and recovered verbatim from the session transcript. V2-3b measured it only on a camera later found inside a building, so it was never judged on a valid view.
changes_from_origin: The expected occupancy is clamped to [0, 1]. The original 1 - occupancy_threshold is -0.1 for the National Assembly facade, whose 1.1 threshold means never lit, and would have emitted negative light wherever the fade engaged.
known_approximations: The expected curtain and blind factors assume their phases are uniform over the whole cell, but they only matter where the pane covers the cell, so the product of the separate means is not exactly the mean of the product.
